title: The New-born Child of Gospel-grace
description: The New-born Child of Gospel-grace in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 68, “The new convert”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The new born child of gos-pel grace, Like some fair tree when sum-mer's nigh, Be-neath Em-ma-nuel's shin-ing face, Lifts up his bloom-ing branch on high.

lines: The new-born child of gospel-grace,
Like some fair tree when summer's nigh,
Beneath Emmanuel's shining face,
Lifts up his blooming branch on high.
No fears he feels, he sees no foes,
No conflict yet his faith employs,
Nor has he learnt to whom he owes,
The strength and peace his soul enjoys.
But sin soon darts its cruel sting,
And comforts sinking day by day;
What seemed his own, a self-fed spring,
Proves but a brook that glides away.
When Gideon armed his num'rous host,
The Lord soon made his numbers less;
And said, lest Israel vainly boast,
"My arm procured me this success."
Thus will he bring our spirits down,
And draw our ebbing comforts low;
That saved by grace, but not our own,
We may not claim the praise we owe.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
